description: We are The Bio-Telemetry Crew, an independent Biotechnology-led initiative tackling the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Combining clinical optometry science with rapid software prototyping, we built FarSight—a non-invasive, camera-based near-point screening and Focus Reserve tool to monitor Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) during deep-space missions.
summary:
FarSight is a non-invasive visual screening and decision-support web application designed to monitor Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) during long-duration space missions. On deep-space voyages to Mars lasting over 1,200 days, communication delays with Earth can reach 40 minutes, requiring astronauts to independently assess and manage changes in their near vision.

Built on optometric physics and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) risk models, FarSight converts near-point focusing distance into accommodation power (diopters) and evaluates personal Focus Reserve across critical mission tasks—including 30 cm medical kit labels, 40 cm tablet checklists, 60 cm control panels, and 25 cm fine work—using Green, Amber, and Red safety thresholds. The platform features five interactive modules: a constant angular-size Near-Point Screening Test, a Mission Day 90 Crew Trend Dashboard, an Adaptive Procedure Reader that scales text to comfortable viewing distances, a "See What They See" defocus blur simulator for flight surgeons, and a Pre-Flight Mars Glasses Planner that calculates exact +0.25 D corrective eyewear packing lists. FarSight is strictly a screening and decision-support tool and does not replace comprehensive clinical eye exams.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Long-duration missions expose astronauts to fluid shifts and microgravity hazards that can trigger Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), causing hyperopic shifts that make close-up tasks—such as reading emergency medication dosage cards or tablet checklists—difficult or unsafe. On deep-space missions to Mars (up to 1,224 days), communication delays with Earth can reach 40 minutes, requiring crew members to independently assess and manage changes in their near vision.

FarSight is an interactive, non-invasive clinical screening and decision-support application built around five core modules:

1. Near-Point Visual Screening Test: Uses constant angular-size targets (8.6 arcmin scaling) and camera/near-point input to measure accommodation amplitude in diopters (D = 100 / cm) and evaluate personal Focus Reserve across critical mission tasks (40 cm tablet checklists, 30 cm medical kit labels, 60 cm control panels, and 25 cm fine work) using Green (>= 100%), Amber (50-99%), and Red (< 50%) safety thresholds.

2. Crew Dashboard & Forecast: Tracks longitudinal focusing power against pre-flight baselines (modeled via Hofstetter's age formula) across simulated crew profiles through Mission Day 90, triggering automated Flight Surgeon alerts when sustained hyperopic drops exceed clinical thresholds.

3. Adaptive Procedure Reader: Calculates optimal comfortable reading distance (200 / D) and dynamically scales procedure checklist text to prevent eye strain.

4. "See What They See" Blur Simulator: Generates a geometric defocus blur preview (4 mm pupil, 500 mm viewing distance) of a 30 cm emergency medication label so flight surgeons can visualize the astronaut's functional visual deficit.

5. Pre-Flight Mars Glasses Planner: Models normal age-related drift (0.3 D/year) across mission durations (30-day LEO/Lunar, 365-day ISS/Lunar, and 1,224-day Mars planetary missions) under 0 D, +0.75 D, and +2.00 D SANS shift scenarios to generate an exact +0.25 D step pre-flight corrective eyewear packing list.

Benefits, Intended Impact & Creativity:

FarSight turns standard onboard screens and cameras into an autonomous ocular triage tool without bulky ophthalmic hardware. Beyond protecting astronaut safety on Artemis and Mars missions, FarSight's offline-ready screening workflow can bring rapid, accessible presbyopia screening to remote and underserved communities on Earth.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

Developed in Python using Streamlit for interactive web deployment, NumPy and Pandas for physiological modeling and focus-reserve calculations, Plotly for longitudinal telemetry charts, and Pillow (PIL) for optical defocus blur simulation. Hosted publicly on GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud.

Clinical Safety & Factors Considered:

We prioritized human-factors clarity (color-coded status indicators, large scannable metrics, zero-clutter navigation) and strict clinical safety boundaries: FarSight is explicitly designed as a screening and decision-support tool and does not diagnose eye disease or replace comprehensive clinical eye exams.
